Exact-head independent semantic/code review: CHANGES REQUIRED

Audited head: `868a6111eb592a038b806a02c828b3ffb17971be`
Tree: `38eacdb971042c0a748f780bb634766933543f61`
Base/predecessor: `92044d305e5340e31df766bf10e9f60f0feebe07`
Predecessor tree: `7c32a23ab0af1f82dcf54b90fb6ec6a3156a855d`

The semantic shard itself is internally consistent: independent recomputation passed 79/72/7 scope conservation, all 117 terminal score-owning parts, 111 primary plus 22 secondary classifications, 133 approved core plus 3 supporting candidate instances, 5 isolated unmodeled Numerical Solution parts, 17 cumulative models, 497 records, exact QP/MS evidence, predecessor object preservation, raw-byte custody/runtime pins, graph integrity, and candidate isolation. The source-text review also supports the six Differentiation model families and the Trigonometry/Integration/Numerical Solution ownership lanes.

However, three exact-head findings remain unresolved:

1. Blocking successor-custody gap: the new multi-generation successor branch in `validate_checked_release` validates reconstructed manifest lineage and immediately returns older gates, but never authenticates the checked active output paths against the active manifest records. Therefore an active nodes/edges/registry/composition byte drift can still make the older `--check` commands report PASS. Preserve the generic chain validation, then authenticate every active manifest-bound output file and fail closed on missing, length-drifted, or hash-drifted bytes before returning success. See https://github.com/Samsen879/ciecopilot-home/pull/1735#discussion_r3660310161.

2. Published metric correctness: `model_usage` counts core ProcedureInstances, not distinct questions. `9709.procedure.differentiation.solve_stationary_point` is reported as 28 questions, but independent recomputation finds 28 instances across 27 distinct `question_id` values because `qrow_9709_s19_qp_33_q07` uses the model on parts ii and iii. This inflates `questions_per_procedure_model` and `procedure_reuse_ratio`. Derive question-named metrics from distinct question identities and add a repeated-model-within-one-question regression. See https://github.com/Samsen879/ciecopilot-home/pull/1735#discussion_r3660310155.

3. Replay scalability: the generic validator rebuilds each current issue and then its predecessor, then rebuilds that predecessor again on the next loop. The focused successor-chain test took 232.754 seconds locally before the sequential checks. Cache generated manifests/build results by issue for the validation duration or otherwise reuse each predecessor result once. See https://github.com/Samsen879/ciecopilot-home/pull/1735#discussion_r3660310151.

Verification completed at this exact tree:

- issue #1725 Python suite: 9/9 passed
- generic multi-generation successor test: passed in 232.754s
- issue #1722/#1723/#1724/#1725 deterministic checks: currently report PASS
- service, API, and real gateway Jest: 49/49 passed
- independent exhaustive runtime probe: 362 approved instances across 331 parts, 111 new primary mappings, 3 candidates, and 5 unavailable parts all matched
- targeted ESLint, Python compilation, and `git diff --check`: PASS

The passing older `--check` outputs do not close finding 1 because that is the false-negative path under review. CI remains separate, and this COMMENTED receipt grants no merge, release, or subsequent-stage authority.

Predecessor tree: `7c32a23ab0af1f82dcf54b90fb6ec6a3156a855d`

The three blockers from the prior `868a6111eb` review are repaired at this head:

- Active-manifest custody now authenticates all 8 output records from raw bytes and fails closed on missing files, length drift, and equal-length SHA drift; the end-to-end older-check tamper regression also passed.
- The stationary-point metric now reports 28 instances across 27 distinct questions and the cumulative reuse ratio is 28.0.
- The validation-scoped cache eliminates repeated direct lookups in the chain loop, and the isolated real-chain regression improved from 232.754s to 170.640s.

However, the final live-thread gate exposed two new exact-head blockers, and both reproduce independently:

1. Blocking scope omission: `discover_scope` compares the source-map `question_key` literally with canonical graph IDs. Its seven excluded Differentiation rows are exactly the seven `qrow_WM_...` rows. Removing that filename-origin prefix maps every row to an existing canonical `Question` with `verification_state: resolver_verified`. Those canonical questions contain 10 score-owning parts, and every one has both QP and MS `SUPPORTED_BY` evidence, but none appears in `semantic-registry.json`. The hard-coded 79/72/7 conservation therefore turns an identity-format mismatch into an unsupported semantic exclusion and leaves those product readbacks unavailable. Normalize the source-map identity before the verified join, review/classify the resulting 10 parts, rebuild the release, and add a regression covering the WM-to-canonical join. See https://github.com/Samsen879/ciecopilot-home/pull/1735#discussion_r3660576824.

2. Successor replay is still recursively redundant: the new cache wraps only direct `get_generated_manifest` calls. Each cached successor `build_release` still calls `authenticated_predecessor`, which recursively rebuilds older releases; the next separately loaded successor repeats those builds. The focused mock only counts outer loader calls and cannot observe this recursion. This does not satisfy the requested each-successor-once property and still scales quadratically as the release chain grows. Propagate a shared build cache through predecessor construction or return/reuse the manifests already produced by the first recursive build, then instrument a real nested chain rather than only the outer loader. See https://github.com/Samsen879/ciecopilot-home/pull/1735#discussion_r3660576813.

Verification on this exact tree:

- issue #1725 suite: 10/10 passed

- focused cache, distinct-question metric, and missing/length/hash custody regressions: passed
- end-to-end #1724 successor byte-tamper regression: passed
- service/API/real-gateway Jest: 49/49 passed
- independent custody/metric probe: 8 authenticated outputs; 28 instances/27 questions; missing, length, and hash drift all rejected
- issue #1722 and #1723 standalone deterministic checks: PASS; #1724 covered through its end-to-end successor validator; #1725 full deterministic suite passed
- targeted ESLint, Python compilation, and `git diff --check`: PASS

The original semantic invariants remain internally consistent for the currently selected 72-question shard, but they do not make the seven alias-omitted questions valid exclusions. CI is still queued and remains separate. This COMMENTED receipt grants no merge, release, or subsequent-stage authority.

The two blockers from the `8ed433ef7a` review are repaired at this head:

- All seven `qrow_WM_...` source aliases normalize collision-free to resolver-verified canonical Questions. Independent artifact traversal found exactly 10 recovered score-owning QuestionParts, each with one terminal approved-primary decision, exact part-level QP and MS anchors, the expected primary/secondary types, and approved core procedures. The two material trigonometric equation steps remain supporting candidates at sequence 3 and are never exposed as approved. The shard now conserves 79/79 questions, 127 reviewed parts, 121 primary plus 26 secondary classifications, 147 approved core instances, 5 supporting candidates, and 504 cumulative records.
- Independent wrapping of the real nested #1722→#1725 build path recorded exactly one `build_release` call per issue, matching the shared cache counters `{1722: 1, 1723: 1, 1724: 1, 1725: 1}` in 20.035 seconds. The complete lineage and active raw-byte custody checks still ran.

One blocking metric defect remains:

`issue_1725_differentiation_semantic_kg.py` correctly deduplicates the new Differentiation models, but then inherits the predecessor `questions_per_procedure_model` values unchanged. The #1724 Trigonometry builder produced those values with an instance `Counter`. `qrow_9709_s18_qp_33_q05::q05/i` has both primary and alternative approved core instances of `9709.procedure.trigonometry.prove_identity`, so the active procedure library reports 13 questions for that model while the #1724 delta contains only 12 distinct `question_id` values. The published cumulative `procedure_reuse_ratio` is consequently `28.823529`; independently recomputing the question-named metrics from the #1719 baseline plus distinct IDs in the #1723/#1724/#1725 deltas yields `28.764706`. Fix or normalize the predecessor metric at its source, rebuild all manifest-bound outputs/runtime pins, and add a regression for multiple branches of one model within one question.
